q1: SELECT beer, MAX(price) - MIN(price) AS price_gap, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM serves WHERE beer IN (SELECT s.beer FROM serves AS s, frequents AS f WHERE s.bar = f.bar AND f.drinker LIKE 'B%' GROUP BY s.beer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.bar) >= 2) GROUP BY beer ORDER BY beer
q2: WITH BarFreq AS (SELECT DISTINCT bar FROM frequents WHERE drinker LIKE 'B%'), beerServed AS (SELECT s.beer, s.bar, s.price FROM serves AS s WHERE s.bar IN (SELECT bar FROM BarFreq)), beerServedCount AS (SELECT beer, COUNT(bar) AS barCount FROM beerServed GROUP BY beer HAVING COUNT(bar) >= 2) SELECT bs.beer, MAX(bs.price) - MIN(bs.price) AS price_gap, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM beerServed AS bs JOIN beerServedCount AS bsc ON bs.beer = bsc.beer GROUP BY bs.beer

explanation: Q1 includes all serves for beers that meet the bar frequency condition, while Q2 only considers serves in bars that meet the frequency condition. This leads to different aggregate calculations when a beer is served in both qualifying and non-qualifying bars.
counterexample_dsp: A beer served in two bars frequented by 'B%' drinkers and one non-frequented bar. Q1 includes all three serves, Q2 only includes the two in frequented bars, leading to different price gaps and averages.
